findings.recommendation: Lazy order: (1) Put the 'by hand' cases where the Manager will see them. Write the paid-late or refund-failed case to an existing table (audit_log, or a payments status), and show a count on /manage/orders. Logs are not a work queue. (2) Add src/instrumentation.ts with onRequestError that forwards to a free error tracker (Sentry's free tier, for example) or at least emits one structured JSON line. (3) Add a tiny GET /api/health that runs `SELECT 1`, and point a free uptime monitor at it. Write the three into docs/06-SETUP.md section 9.

findings.title: No backup or restore plan for the production database, and Production builds migrate it with no snapshot first
findings.evidence: vercel.json:3: `if [ "$VERCEL_ENV" = "production" ]; then prisma migrate deploy; fi && next build`. Every Production build applies pending migrations to Neon directly. grep -i 'backup|restore|point-in-time' across docs/ finds only ADR 0014's 'No backup codes'. Neon's plans page (fetched 2026-11-10): 'Instant restore is free on the Free plan for up to 6 hours of history, limited to 1 GB of change history per project.' Nothing in section 9 tells the owner how to restore, or to branch the database before a risky migration.
findings.impact: A bad migration, a mistaken SQL edit in the Neon console (section 9 step 5 already sends the owner there for `UPDATE users SET role`), or a bug that deletes rows can be undone only if noticed within 6 hours. After that the Orders, Stars ledger and Members are gone. On a real cafe that means Stars balances (ADR 0008) and sales records.
findings.recommendation: Add a short 'Backups and restore' step to section 9. (1) Before merging a PR that has a migration, create a Neon branch of production as a snapshot (one click, or `neonctl branches create`). (2) Know where the restore-to-time screen is and that its window is 6 hours on Free. (3) Optionally, a weekly `pg_dump` of the direct URL from the owner's computer to the G: drive. For a real cafe, a paid Neon plan (1-day history or more) is the cheap fix.

findings.title: Migrations land before the new code and outlive a rollback, with no rule that they stay compatible with the running deployment
findings.evidence: The buildCommand runs `prisma migrate deploy` and only then `next build`. The new schema is live for the whole build, and stays live if `next build` fails, while the previous deployment keeps serving. Vercel's Instant Rollback switches code back without rebuilding, so it never reverts a migration. Nothing in the docs states an expand-then-contract rule. A real example: migration 20261108014735 added event_signups.confirmed_at and back-filled only existing rows (`UPDATE "event_signups" SET "confirmed_at" = "created_at"`). A Sign-up the old code took during that build has confirmed_at NULL. The new heldSignups() (signups.ts:17: `OR: [{ confirmedAt: { not: null } }, { createdAt: { gt: holdStart(at) } }]`) stops holding its Seats 30 minutes later, and its email had no confirm link. The migrations so far are additive, so nothing broke, but nothing prevents a DROP or RENAME next time.
findings.impact: A migration that drops, renames or tightens a column breaks the live site for the length of the build. If the build fails, it stays broken until a fix deploys. A rollback after a bad deploy then pairs old code with the new schema. The window is small on a demo, but it hits real Orders on a real cafe.
findings.recommendation: Write the rule into docs/06-SETUP.md section 9 and CLAUDE.md: migrations must work with the previous release (add first; drop or rename only in a later release once no code reads the column), and a rollback past a migration needs a forward fix. Optionally move `prisma migrate deploy` after a successful build, so a failed build leaves the schema alone: `next build && { [ "$VERCEL_ENV" != production ] || prisma migrate deploy; }`. Prerendering reads the DB at build time, so this needs the expand-first rule anyway.

findings.title: No CI and no dependency update bot: quality gates run only when someone remembers, and advisories are found by hand
findings.evidence: The repo has no .github folder, so there are no GitHub Actions, no dependabot.yml and no Renovate config. The only automatic check on push is Vercel's build: `prisma migrate deploy` (production) then `next build`, which type-checks but does not lint and runs no tests. The 228 Vitest tests, 180 Playwright tests, Prettier, ESLint and `npm audit` run only through the manual `npm run qa` / `qa:full`. better-auth sat 6 patch releases behind a security release until the audit found it (ID1-17, SEC1-11). `npm outdated` could not even be measured today (gates/outdated.log: 'npm error code ECONNRESET').
findings.impact: A pull request can merge red: failing tests, lint or e2e. The owner merges on GitHub, and Vercel deploys main straight to production, migrating the database on the way. Security releases of next, better-auth, pg or prisma surface only when someone happens to look. GitHub is the project's only copy and is public, which makes it a showcase where green checks matter.
findings.recommendation: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml on pull_request: a postgres:17 service, `npm ci`, then lint, format:check, typecheck, `vitest run` against a `_test` database and `npm audit --omit=dev`. Playwright can run nightly or on label to save minutes. Add .github/dependabot.yml for npm (weekly, grouped minor and patch, separate PRs for majors) and github-actions. Turn on branch protection for main with the CI check required.

findings.title: Environment variables are never validated at startup; several fail open to localhost, an empty key or the Resend test sender
findings.evidence: Each variable is read where it is used, and the fallbacks disagree. Six places use `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL ?? "http://localhost:3000"`: links.ts:25 (Order links in emails), layout.tsx:32 (metadataBase and share cards), cafe/page.tsx:111 (structured data), events actions.ts:81, calendar route.ts:11 and fake.ts:20. second-factor.ts:20 has `const key = () => process.env.BETTER_AUTH_SECRET ?? ""`. outbox.ts:27 falls back to `Hoshikopi <onboarding@resend.dev>`, and outbox.ts:38 decides on `process.env.VERCEL` whether links are logged. A missing CRON_SECRET makes route.ts:15 answer 401 forever, with no error. The payment provider fails closed (provider.ts:33-45), but only on first use. place.ts:323-336 then catches the throw after the Order is committed: `console.error("[payments] checkout not started:", error); return { ok: false, reason: "payment_start_failed" }`. The Order holds its Pickup Window for 15 minutes. Nothing validates the set as a whole: no src/lib/env.ts, no instrumentation register(), no check in next.config.ts. zod is already a dependency.
findings.impact: A Production deploy with a missing or mistyped variable builds and goes live. The fault shows only per request. Emails carry localhost links. Second Factor secrets get encrypted with an empty key (ID1-12). The cron silently never runs. Every online checkout creates an Order that holds Capacity and then fails, while the trace sits in a log kept for 1 hour.
findings.recommendation: One small src/lib/env.ts: a zod schema for the server variables (required in production: DATABASE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET of 32+ characters, BETTER_AUTH_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL as an https URL, CRON_SECRET, PAYMENT_PROVIDER, plus the provider-specific keys) and an exported parsed object. Call it from next.config.ts when VERCEL_ENV is 'production', so a misconfigured deploy fails its build and the old one stays live. Replace the `?? localhost` fallbacks with the parsed value. Skip a config framework; the schema is about 30 lines.

findings.title: Emails are sent inline with no timeout or retry: a slow Resend would stall Bar Screen taps, webhook replies and checkout
findings.evidence: outbox.ts:20 calls `fetch("https://api.resend.com/emails", {...})` with no `signal`. Node's fetch has no overall timeout; undici's header and body timeouts default to 300 s, and Hobby's function limit is 300 s. Callers await it in the request path. In transition() at status.ts:131: `if (to === "ready") await emailOrderReady(orderId);`, and the Bar Screen's Ready tap goes through transition. webhook.ts:58 awaits emailOrderPlaced before the webhook answers 200. place.ts:321 awaits it for Pay at Pickup before checkout returns. refund.ts:48 does the same. attempt() (emails.ts) catches errors, but it cannot cut a hang short. When Resend refuses, outbox.ts:34 keeps only the status code: `Resend refused the email: ${response.status}`. Resend's reason text is dropped, and that text is what explains the test-sender restriction a first Resend setup hits. No retry exists, so a failed confirmation or Ready email is lost. On the demo today RESEND_API_KEY is unset, so this is dormant.
findings.impact: On the first deploy with Resend, any Resend slowdown makes the barista's Ready tap spin for seconds or minutes, and the board falls behind. Webhook replies slow down, so PayMongo retries. Checkout for Pay at Pickup hangs. Debugging a 403 from Resend needs its message, which is never logged.
findings.recommendation: Add `signal: AbortSignal.timeout(5000)` to the Resend fetch and log `await response.text()` (it carries no secret) with the status. In the Server Actions and route handlers that trigger emails, run the email in `after()` from next/server (after.md: usable in Server Functions and Route Handlers), so the response is not blocked. Keep transition() itself free of after(), because it also runs in the cron and in tests. Retries can wait until a real domain exists; say so in a ponytail comment.

findings.title: The image optimizer accepts any party's Vercel Blob store under /menu/, so anyone can spend the Hobby image-transformation quota
findings.evidence: next.config.ts:34-35: `hostname: "*.public.blob.vercel-storage.com", pathname: "/menu/**"`. The wildcard matches every Blob store on Vercel, not just hoshikopi-photos. Live probe with a made-up store: GET /_next/image?url=https://auditnotarealstore.public.blob.vercel-storage.com/menu/x.jpg&w=640&q=75 gave 404 'NOT_FOUND'. The optimizer accepted the URL and fetched upstream. The same host with /other/x.jpg gave 400 'INVALID_IMAGE_OPTIMIZE_REQUEST' (refused by the allowlist). Vercel's Hobby page (fetched 2026-11-10) lists 'Image Transformations: First 5,000' and says 'if you exceed your usage limits on the Hobby plan, you will have to wait until 30 days have passed before you can use the feature again.'
findings.impact: Anyone with a free Vercel account can put images under menu/ in their own Blob store and request them through hoshikopi.vercel.app/_next/image with each allowed width. Every new source image costs Hoshikopi transformations, and 5,000 is quickly gone. After that, the site's own Menu Item photos (once real ones land) stop being optimized for up to 30 days. Exactly how Vercel enforces it (failed images, or a paused project) is not confirmed. It also lets the site act as an image proxy for other people's content.
findings.recommendation: Pin the hostname to this store's own host, `<store-id>.public.blob.vercel-storage.com`, which is visible in the first real upload's URL or the Blob dashboard. A literal string is enough; no config variable is needed. Re-run the probe above: it should then answer 400.

findings.title: Still present on the live demo: seeded Event, Promo and seasonal dates are running out (Latte art night is already past)
findings.evidence: Live, 2026-11-10. /events lists 'Past Events Latte art night Sat, Nov 7, 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM', and its .ics has DTSTART:20261107T110000Z. The only upcoming one-off Event, on /events and on Home's 'Upcoming event', is 'Open mic under the stars, Sat, Nov 21'. /menu/item/matcha-latte shows 'Promo until Tue, Dec 1'. The weekly Recurring Events (Latte art practice on Wednesdays, Open mic on Thursdays) keep /events from going empty, but they are a plain list with no Sign-up (schema RecurringEvent has no relation to event_signups). seed.ts:25-28 still refuses a second run ('Already seeded'), and nothing refreshes the dates.
findings.impact: From Nov 22 Home loses its Upcoming event card, and the Event Sign-up flow (EVT-02, with its hold and confirmation built in 8.7) cannot be shown on the live demo. From Dec 2 the Promo badge disappears. Around Dec 30 Calamansi Honey Soda turns Hidden, and the Tapa Rice Bowl's pairing points at an item that is off the menu. Phase 9's portfolio review happens after these dates.
findings.recommendation: As DATA-03, but smaller now that a daily cron exists. In /api/cron/daily (or a script run with ALLOW_REMOTE_SEED), roll the two seeded Events forward by whole weeks while they are past and still carry their seeded slug, title and summary, and roll the seeded Promo and available_until forward the same way. Rows a Manager has edited stay untouched. Or, more simply, have the Manager add new Events in /manage/events now and diarise it.

findings.title: The daily cron does no housekeeping: rate-limit keys (emails and IPs), guest Carts and expired verifications pile up
findings.evidence: The cron still does only `expireUnpaid(now())` and `revalidateTag("menu", "max")` (route.ts:18-19). grep finds no delete of rate_limits or expired verifications, and no purge of old guest carts, anywhere in src. In the dev DB today: rate_limits 143 rows (2026-11-05 06:00 to 2026-11-09 23:45 UTC; keys hold emails such as `link:<email>` and IPs), guest carts 83, verifications 3. On timing: Vercel's cron page says Hobby precision is 'Per-hour (±59 min)', so `0 22 * * *` fires between 6:00 and 6:59 AM Manila. The seeded 7:00 AM opening is safe, but the 'at 6:00 AM' wording in docs/06 section 9 and docs/03 section 12 is not exact.
findings.impact: Tables grow without bound, faster under abuse, against Neon Free's 0.5 GB. Personal data (emails, IPs) is kept with no retention rule (DATA-09). If a Manager ever moves opening to 6:00 AM, the menu refresh can land after opening; Sold Out is date-keyed, so only the cached page lags.
findings.recommendation: Add three deletes to the cron (each idempotent): rate_limits older than 1 day, verifications past expires_at, and guest carts not updated for 30 days (the cookie's maxAge). Change the docs to 'between 6:00 and 6:59 AM Manila (Hobby fires within the hour)'.

findings.title: The function region (sin1) lives only in the Vercel dashboard; vercel.json and the setup checklist do not pin it
findings.evidence: Live, every dynamic response carries `X-Vercel-Id: sin1::sin1::...` (for example /events/latte-art-night/calendar and /api/orders/<uuid>/status), so functions run in Singapore. /api/orders/<random uuid>/status, which makes one DB query before answering 404, took 0.25 to 0.34 s. /api/bar signed out, with no DB query, took 0.27 to 0.51 s. The database is therefore co-located, and DATA-01's cross-region timeout risk is not live. But vercel.json has no `regions` key, and section 9 never says to set the region. Vercel's default for new projects is iad1 (Washington, D.C.).
findings.impact: Re-importing the project, or creating a second one (for a real cafe), silently puts functions in iad1, 200+ ms per query from Neon in Singapore. placeOrder's roughly 26 statements inside one transaction, with Prisma's default 5 s timeout and no explicit timeout set, then risk P2028 again.
findings.recommendation: Add `"regions": ["sin1"]` to vercel.json (Hobby allows one region), and a line in section 9 step 3. Optionally give placeOrder's $transaction an explicit `{ timeout: 10_000 }` as a margin.

findings.title: Preview deployments are wired to production: same auth URL, site URL and Blob store, and the same database unless Neon branching is on
findings.evidence: Section 9 step 3 says to 'set these variables for Production and Preview', including `BETTER_AUTH_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` = `https://<project>.vercel.app` (line 141) and the Neon DATABASE_URL. Line 130: 'Preview builds share the production database unless the Neon integration gives each preview its own branch'. ADR 0004, by contrast, says Neon 'holds production and preview databases'. Step 6 connects the Blob store to 'Production, Preview and Development'. auth.ts sets no baseURL or trustedOrigins, so Better Auth uses BETTER_AUTH_URL, the production host, on previews. Better Auth 1.7 supports a dynamic `baseURL: { allowedHosts: [...] }` (create-context.mjs checks `allowedHosts`). Whether preview branching is on cannot be seen from here.
findings.impact: On a preview, sign-in links and Order links (NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL is inlined at build) point at production. Unless Neon branching is on, a preview running unmerged code places Orders, writes Stars and audit rows, and uploads photos into production data. Previews are the place a broken migration-free change would be tried.
findings.recommendation: Confirm in the Neon integration that each Preview gets its own branch, and record the fact in section 9. Then fix ADR 0004 or section 9 so they agree. For previews, leave BETTER_AUTH_URL unset and pass `baseURL: { allowedHosts: ["hoshikopi-*.vercel.app"] }` (scoped to this project's preview pattern, not all of vercel.app). Or state plainly that sign-in does not work on previews. Connect Blob to Production only, or accept that preview uploads land in the same store.

findings.title: Better Auth's built-in rate limiter counts in memory, so on serverless each function instance has its own counters
findings.evidence: auth.ts:38 sets `rateLimit: { window: 60, max: 60 }` for magic-link verification. auth.ts sets no rateLimit.storage and no secondaryStorage. create-context.mjs:175 shows the default: `storage: options.rateLimit?.storage || (options.secondaryStorage ? "secondary-storage" : "memory")`, and the limiter is `enabled: ... ?? isProduction`. The app's own limits (sign-in sends, checkout, webhooks, Second Factor) are in Postgres (rate-limit.ts) and are fine.
findings.impact: Low. Better Auth's per-IP limits on its HTTP routes (verify, callback, get-session and the rest) reset on every cold start and are multiplied by the number of concurrent instances, so they protect less than the comment in auth.ts implies. The 32-character link token makes brute force impractical anyway.
findings.recommendation: Either set `rateLimit: { storage: "database" }` and add Better Auth's rateLimit table in a migration, or keep memory and add a ponytail comment that the real limits live in rate-limit.ts and Better Auth's are best-effort per instance.

findings.title: The pg pool has serverless defaults: no connection timeout, and no idle-pool handling for Vercel Fluid compute
findings.evidence: db.ts:8: `new PrismaClient({ adapter: new PrismaPg({ connectionString }) })`. The adapter builds `new pg2.Pool(this.config)` with only the connection string, so pg-pool's defaults apply: max 10, idleTimeoutMillis 10000 (index.js:98), and no connectionTimeoutMillis (index.js:206, which waits forever). @vercel/functions (with attachDatabasePool, Vercel's helper that closes idle pool clients before an instance suspends) is not installed. Whether Fluid compute is on cannot be seen without the dashboard (it is the default for new projects). I saw no errors in the requests I made.
findings.impact: If Neon's pooler or compute drops idle sockets while a Fluid instance is suspended, the first query after resume can fail with 'Connection terminated unexpectedly'. Neon scales to zero after 5 minutes, which makes this likelier. A database that is unreachable makes requests wait until the 300 s function limit instead of failing fast. Unconfirmed in practice; the risk is low.
findings.recommendation: Pass a pool config: `new PrismaPg({ connectionString, connectionTimeoutMillis: 5_000, idleTimeoutMillis: 5_000, max: 5 })`. If 'Connection terminated' ever shows up in the logs, add @vercel/functions' attachDatabasePool with an external pg.Pool. Until then, skip the dependency.

findings.title: Open status pages and the Bar Screen poll forever, which keeps Neon Free from scaling to zero and can use up its 100 CU-hours
findings.evidence: The status poller polls every 5 s (15 s hidden) until Ready, then every 30 s, and stops only when the Order closes (status-poller.tsx:98-113). Pay at Pickup Orders that nobody moves are never closed (ORD-13), so a forgotten tab polls indefinitely; so does a signed-in Bar Screen (every 3 s). Each poll is a DB query. Neon's plans page: 'Computes suspend after 5 minutes of inactivity', and the Free plan includes '100 CU-hours/project/month' (about 400 hours at 0.25 CU). When the allowance is used up, 'your compute is suspended until the next billing period'. A compute kept awake around the clock at 0.25 CU uses about 180 CU-hours a month.
findings.impact: One status tab or Bar Screen left open for about 17 days (or several left open for less) can suspend the database for the rest of the month. Every dynamic part of the demo (Cart, checkout, sign-in, Orders) then fails. Actual use cannot be checked without the Neon dashboard.
findings.recommendation: Check CU-hour use in the Neon console now. Stop the status poller when the Order's service day has ended, or after a fixed time such as 3 hours. Have the Bar Screen stop polling outside opening hours. Mention the allowance in section 9.

findings.title: Menu photos go to a public Blob store as uploaded (EXIF kept) and before validation, and replaced or refused uploads are never deleted
findings.evidence: photo.ts:63 calls `put(`menu/${name}`, Buffer.from(bytes), { access: "public", ... })` with the raw upload bytes. Nothing strips metadata, so a phone photo's EXIF GPS goes along. actions.ts:71-75 stores the photo, then calls saveMenuItem. A save refused by validation (a bad price, say) leaves the Blob behind, and a file input cannot be kept, so every retry uploads another copy. No `del` from @vercel/blob is imported anywhere (grep: photo.ts only imports `put`), so a replaced photo stays in the store. next/image (photo.tsx) serves resized copies without metadata, but its srcset carries the original public Blob URL in the `url=` parameter, so the original file is one click away. Not yet live: the first real upload is still pending (roadmap 5.4).
findings.impact: A Manager who snaps a photo at home or in the cafe publishes the location. The store collects orphans against the Hobby Blob allowance. Low for a concept site, real for a real cafe.
findings.recommendation: Validate the form before uploading (move storeMenuPhoto after the zod parse, or parse first). When saveMenuItem replaces a photo, `del` the old Blob URL if it is in this store. For EXIF, either re-encode on upload, or ask Managers to export photos without location and say so in the upload hint. Do not add an image library just for this.

findings.title: No Node version is pinned: no engines field and no .nvmrc, and the docs give three different versions
findings.evidence: package.json has no `engines`, and the repo has no .nvmrc, .node-version or .tool-versions. Local `node -v` gives v24.18.0. docs/06-SETUP.md:9 says '22.12 or newer (this computer has 24)', and docs/08-TOOLING.md:63 says 'Node 24.19.0'. Prisma 7 requires '^20.19 || ^22.12 || >=24.0' (node_modules/prisma/package.json:42), and @types/node is ^24. Vercel picks the Node major from `engines.node` if present, otherwise from the project setting, which I cannot see.
findings.impact: Production may run a different Node major than development and CI (once CI exists). Behaviour differences show up only on the live site, and a dashboard change or re-import can silently move the version.
findings.recommendation: Add `"engines": { "node": "24.x" }` to package.json (Vercel honours it) and correct the two doc lines. An .nvmrc is optional.

findings.title: Setup section 9 is not the path the live deploy took, and it leaves out region, Node, logs, backups, previews and the cron window
findings.evidence: Step 1 says to create the Neon project and 'copy two URLs', and step 3 says to set DATABASE_URL and DIRECT_URL by hand. The live project uses Neon through the Vercel integration, which injects DATABASE_URL and DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED itself. Only step 4's aside and line 130 mention it. Missing from the checklist: the function region (sin1, see the region finding); the Node version; that Hobby keeps runtime logs 1 hour (step 5 relies on Logs); backups and the 6-hour restore window; that Hobby crons fire anywhere within the hour; whether Neon preview branching is actually on; and the still-pending first Blob upload. Step 8 ('Check: Lighthouse ... and the two-minute demo script') has no recorded result in section 9. DOC-18's leftovers remain: ALLOW_REMOTE_SEED, DATABASE_URL_UNPOOLED and E2E_DATABASE_URL are still missing from the section 5 table.
findings.impact: Rebuilding the deploy from the doc (a second project, a real cafe, or after losing the Vercel project) would not reproduce the live setup, and it would put functions in iad1.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite steps 1 and 3 around the Neon integration (with the manual path as an aside). Add one line each for the region, Node, log retention, backups and restore, the cron window and the preview database status. Add the three missing variables to section 5.

findings.title: The 'outputFileTracingRoot' / 'turbopack.root' warning comes from a stray lockfile in the user's home folder, not from the project
findings.evidence: build.log: 'Warning: Next.js ignored package-lock.json in C:\Users\cjose because it is outside the current Git repository ... set `turbopack.root`'. server-3300.log gives the same text, naming `outputFileTracingRoot`. `ls -la /c/Users/cjose/package*.json` shows a single 84-byte package-lock.json dated Feb 18 2026. Next already ignores it and traces from the repo. Vercel builds from a clean checkout, so the live site is not affected.
findings.impact: None on Vercel. Locally, a noisy warning on every build and start.
findings.recommendation: Delete the stray C:\Users\cjose\package-lock.json, which is the owner's file outside the repo (check that nothing in the home folder needs it). That is better than adding `outputFileTracingRoot`/`turbopack.root` config for a machine-only quirk.

findings.title: The 'Becoming real' list omits the hosting move: Vercel Hobby is non-commercial, so a real cafe needs Pro (crons, logs, drains)
findings.evidence: PRD line 203: 'Becoming real | A real cafe would need a business, BIR receipts, Internet Transactions Act duties, live PayMongo keys, real photos'. Vercel's Hobby page (fetched 2026-11-10): 'the Hobby plan restricts users to non-commercial, personal use only'. It also caps Hobby at one cron a day with per-hour precision, 1 hour of runtime logs and no Drains, which the expiry design (docs/03 section 12) and the monitoring gap above work around. Neon Free's 6-hour restore window and its compute suspension are the database equivalents.
findings.impact: A plan to 'become real without a rebuild' would leave out a required platform upgrade, and the operational limits that drove several design choices.
findings.recommendation: Add to the PRD row: Vercel Pro (commercial use, per-minute crons, longer logs, Drains), a paid Neon plan (longer restore window, no compute cap), Resend with a verified domain, and error monitoring.

findings.title: Live headers differ from local: Vercel adds Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * to prerendered pages and drops X-Powered-By, and COOP is still missing
findings.evidence: Live / and /menu (X-Vercel-Cache: STALE, X-Nextjs-Prerender: 1) and /dev/pay/<uuid> send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. Function-only responses (/events/latte-art-night/calendar) do not. Local `next start` on :3300 sends no ACAO, but does send `X-Powered-By: Next.js` and `Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store`. Vercel sends no X-Powered-By, and sends `Cache-Control: public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`. The CSP, X-Frame-Options, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy and HSTS served live match next.config.ts exactly, with no 'unsafe-eval' in production. No Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy is sent.
findings.impact: Minimal. ACAO * does not allow credentialed reads, so the cookie-dependent header holes cannot be read cross-origin. The earlier audit's 'no CORS headers are sent' and 'X-Powered-By is sent' hold only for the local server.
findings.recommendation: No action for ACAO. Add `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` to the headers list (SEC1-15) and set `poweredByHeader: false` for non-Vercel hosts.

summaries: The database suite is real and mostly strong: 25 files run against the guarded hoshikopi_test Postgres, freeze time through src/lib/clock.ts, and race the main locks (one Cart placed twice, last window room, two tabs spending 9 Stars, two Managers demoting each other, last Event Seats, a Demo Mode double tap). It is wall-clock safe (228/228 normally, at a simulated 23:50 Manila and at 02:00 Manila in March 2027, and in 3 reruns of the 13 concurrency and clock files), and the pg overlapping-query warning is gone. Mutation runs, though, show rules no test protects: Prep Time ignoring the drinks on the bar survives all 66 placement, bar and Prep Time tests, and a Refund taking Stars below zero survives 42 Star and refund tests; an exhaustive 1,026-case probe found transition() matching the docs table, but the repo pins only about 25 of those cases. The e2e flakiness has concrete causes: cafe-wide changes (pause, Busy Mode, a price, a growing Prep Time queue) run in parallel with specs that order, every sign-in rereads an ever-growing data/mail, one ORD-10 check is satisfied by old emails, and the suite stops working after about 21:15 Manila; today's green run was file-order luck. There is no CI.

The only placement test of Prep Time is 'Empty queue: Prep Time 5 minutes, ready 9:05, first window 9:15' (place-order.test.ts:105-111); bar.test.ts says 'Empty queue' too; prepMinutes(4, ...) per-drink maths is unit-tested only. (1) Pause: manage-hours.spec.ts:16-21 pauses ordering cafe-wide; the default is 30 minutes (actions.ts:103 `|| 30`), so if the test dies between Pause and Resume every later Order in the run is refused. (2) Busy Mode vs the first window: bar.spec.ts:114-136 turns on 'Busy +15 min, 1 hour' while bar.spec.ts:9 (same file, same desktop project) taps the FIRST Scheduled window (bar.spec.ts:30-34); placeOrder re-checks a Scheduled window against Prep Time at submit (place.ts:236-243) and the first chip always falls inside +15, so any overlap gives 'window_unavailable'. In e2e.log these two ran together: line 126 'ok 114 ... Busy Mode ... (13.9s)' finished before line 134 'ok 110 ... Phase 2 exit (39.4s)'. (5) Global resets: every beforeEach rewrites capacity_rules and deletes all checkout-ip limits (db.ts:26-34); every signIn deletes all link-ip and second-factor keys (sign-in.ts:29-33); content.spec deletes all signup- keys. Before my runs the folder held 951 files (3.1 MB on disk): 604 carry the frozen Vitest stamp 2026-11-02T01-00-00-000Z although their mtimes are 11-05, 11-06 and 11-10, so DB tests write into the developer's real outbox (about 74 on 11-10 from the gates run); my audit runs took it to 1,512. findings.title: The e2e suite depends on the Manila wall clock: one test fails from about 21:15 and nearly every ordering test from about 23:20, not only after 23:45 as db.ts says
findings.evidence: The server reads the real clock, so openAllDayToday() opens today 00:00 to 23:59 with Last Order 23:45 and says it 'Fails only from 23:45 Manila time' (db.ts:16). But windows are 15 minutes from opening while start + 15 <= closing, so the last starts at 23:30, and the first must be at least now + Prep Time (seed: 4 + 1.5 per queued drink, rounded up to 5; about 10 minutes once order-status.spec leaves a drink 'preparing' in each project). checkout.spec.ts:148-171 needs 6 chips plus option index 2 in Later today (`list.locator("option").nth(2)`, CHIPS = 6), that is 9 windows, so it fails once now + Prep Time passes 21:30, about 21:15 to 21:20 Manila (about 21:05 if Busy Mode is on). From about 23:20 no window is left, so ASAP placement returns no_window and every ordering spec fails; at midnight a test that straddles the day has no Special Hours row for the new day until its next beforeEach. Vitest is safe: the whole suite passed with the clock shifted to 23:50 Manila and to 02:00 Manila (see coverage).
findings.impact: The owner (in Manila) running npm run test:e2e or qa:full in the evening gets red runs unrelated to the code; a scheduled CI run at the wrong UTC hour would fail every night (21:15 Manila is 13:15 UTC).
findings.recommendation: Short term: make the time-sensitive tests count what is offered (the 8.3 test should pick the last option of Later today, and skip with a reason when fewer than 9 windows remain), fix the db.ts comment, and have reset-db.mts refuse to start between 21:00 and 00:30 Manila with a clear message. Better: let the e2e server run on a shifted clock, since clock.ts is the one place that reads now: an offset from an env var honoured only with PAYMENT_PROVIDER=fake and never when VERCEL_ENV is production, set by playwright.config.ts to land at 10:00 Manila, with page.clock set to match. Then openAllDayToday and its Special Hours row go away.

summaries: The architecture holds up well. The nine modules form an acyclic graph: cafe, cart, content, loyalty and menu depend on identity, identity depends on notify, and ordering coordinates cafe, cart, loyalty, notify and payments. No file imports another module's internal/. The lint rule catches 9 of 10 deep-import shapes I probed (all but a dynamic import()). Order Status is written only in status.ts:155. TypeScript is clean: 0 any, 0 ts-ignore, 2 justified eslint-disable lines, and no unused locals or parameters under --noUnusedLocals and --noUnusedParameters. The 40 'use client' files are leaves or forms, and none imports a module value. The one real bug is in the public menu: the Photo stand-in crashes for any Category slug outside its icon map, and Managers can add or rename Categories. Confirmed by rendering Photo with an unknown slug. The rest is about locality. Order Status rules, the Sold Out rule, date conversions, Zod helpers, form results, badge and allergen keys and the Concept Notice are each restated in 3 to 10 places. Module rules that client code needs (max quantity, default Options, Bar Screen types) are copied by hand, because the index.ts files carry server code. Two modules read tables they do not own. Some workflows live in Server Actions instead of modules: Event Sign-up limits, account deletion and inquiries. Neither the result convention in ADR 0001 nor 'Zod at the edge' in docs/03 section 13 matches the code. /manage/cafe and several pages still hand-roll what the 8.10 components (Field, SaveBar, Panel, PageHeader, pills) now do. Refactors ranked by value for effort: (1) give Photo a fallback icon (S); (2) reuse Field, SaveBar, Panel and MarkdownField in cafe-form.tsx, about -90 lines (S); (3) pass orderCodePrefix in OrderingDay and get option names from menu, fixing table ownership (S); (4) add a ConceptNotice component and use the exported constants in copy (S); (5) cache currentCart() per request (S); (6) add a src/lib/forms.ts with fieldErrors, email, slug, checkbox, hhmm, isUniqueClash and FormResult, and align the three result-shape outliers (M); (7) add Order Status helpers in ordering (nextBarStatus, canCustomerCancel, isClosed, refundable, one on-the-bar filter) (M); (8) have the server compute client defaults so option-picker and bar-screen stop copying module rules (M); (9) move the Sign-up and deletion workflows into modules and make Manager-only module writes check the role themselves (M); (10) add clock.ts day helpers and adopt PageHeader, a large pill, StatTile and SavedNotice everywhere (M); (11) split the three oversized page functions (M).

Outliers: second-factor.ts:51 'type SecondFactorResult = "ok" | "wrong" | "too_many"'; photo.ts:33 '{ ok: false; error: string }'; payments.ts:147 'RefundOutcome = "no_online_payment" | "refunded" | "already_refunded"'; save-hours.ts:265 throws 'Busy Mode takes 10 or 15 minutes...' for a refusal; cart.ts:71-72 answers a bad quantity with reason "invalid_options"; refund.ts:62-70 cancelOrder returns the transition result and drops refundOrder's RefundResult; updateQuantity, removeLine, removeFavourite and setInquiryStatus return void. The same form-result type is declared 6 times: FormResult (edit.ts:33), HoursResult (save-hours.ts:11), DetailsResult (save-details.ts:40), ContentResult (content.ts:152), InquiryResult (inquiries.ts:51) and inline in place.ts:64 and signups.ts:73. Convert the outliers: enterSecondFactor returns { ok, reason }, storeMenuPhoto returns { ok: false, errors: { photo } }, startBusyMode returns { ok: false, reason: 'invalid' }, and cancelOrder returns the transition result plus refund. summaries: Staff tools QA on main (0aa0462) against the production build on :3300, as Manager Christian (with and without a fresh Second Factor), Barista Annika and Member Hoshi, at 1280 px and on the Bar Screen at 768 and 1024 px. The core loop works: the Bar Screen polls every 3 s, a new Order shows within 0.3 s with a chime and gold edge, one tap moves it lane to lane with focus on the lane heading, the mute choice survives a reload, a signed-out board says so within 1 s, Busy Mode and Pause change checkout at once, refunds and cancels work, and every Manager-only Server Action I called as a Barista, a Member or signed out was refused (404 or a sign-in redirect). The real problems are at the edges. (1) A Manager without a fresh Second Factor sees Pause, Busy and Cancel on the Bar Screen; a tap leaves the board for /manage/two-factor, the action is dropped, and after the code the shared tablet lands on /manage/hours with a full Manager session. (2) Public freshness is slower than promised: a Sold Out tap took 60.7 s to reach the Menu Item page and hiding an item took 117 s to leave /menu, against 'within seconds' in docs/03. (3) Two screens both labelled Sales disagree (PHP 3,665 on Orders and the Today strip, PHP 3,425 in Reports for the same day). (4) Missing validation: a cleared Capacity cell saves 0 drinks for that weekday with no message, blank map pins save 0,0, and prices above PHP 21,474,836 crash the editor and lose the form. (5) Busy Mode is invisible and unmanageable outside the Bar Screen, and /manage/hours's Prep Time example ignores it. (6) Tools a real cafe needs are missing: no delete or archive for any menu or content record (earlier AUDIT TEST rows from 6 November are still there), no way to remove or contact Event Sign-ups, and no Second Factor status or reset on /manage/staff. Promoting an AUDIT TEST account to Barista was blocked by the session's permission classifier, so the new-Barista enrolment and 'Sign out everywhere' lag were judged from code.
coverage: Read docs/audit/2026-11-06-interim.md (ID1, ID2, DOC-16, PERF-02/03, DATA-02) and every area in docs/audit/findings-2026-11-10.json before testing; ADRs 0005, 0011, 0014 and 0015 checked before flagging.

findings.title: A Manager without a fresh Second Factor sees Pause, Busy and Cancel on the Bar Screen; a tap drops the action, leaves the board and ends on /manage/hours
findings.evidence: bar-screen.tsx renders the Manager controls from `manager={staff.role === "manager"}` only, but their actions call `requireStaff("manager", "/manage/hours")` (hours/actions.ts:27) and cancelAtBar calls `requireStaff("manager", "/manage/orders")`, which redirect without a Second Factor. Observed with a fresh Christian session (no code entered): /bar showed 'Pause ordering 30 min', 'Busy +10 min, 30 min', 'Busy +15 min, 1 hour' and 'Cancel K-018'; tapping Busy +10 navigated to /manage/two-factor?next=%2Fmanage%2Fhours, tapping Cancel this order to /manage/two-factor?next=%2Fmanage%2Forders. After entering the code the browser landed on /manage/hours and cafe_settings still had busy_minutes 0, busy_until null. Roadmap 8.10 lists 'the Bar Screen Second Factor redirect, a bug listed for its own fix', but no saved finding describes this outcome.
findings.impact: In a rush the Manager taps Busy or Pause, loses the board, enters a code on the shared tablet, and ends on a different page with nothing applied, so the very action meant to keep times honest silently did not happen. The shared bar tablet then holds a full Manager session (Refunds, Stars, Staff).
findings.recommendation: Render the Manager controls only when the session has the Second Factor (pass `secondFactor` from the page, or check in BarScreen), or show them disabled with 'Enter your code on Manage first'. If kept, redirect back to /bar and re-apply the tapped action after the code. Add an e2e test for a Manager without a Second Factor on /bar.

refs: findings-2026-11-10 tests: MENU-04's e2e check waits up to 150 s
findings.title: Public menu takes about a minute or two to show a Sold Out or a Hidden item, not 'within seconds'
findings.evidence: Timed with my own AUDIT TEST item, one change at a time, polling the public page every 1 s (scratch/staff/menu4.mjs): unhide -> on /menu after 285 ms; Sold out (8 s after the previous save) -> /menu/item/audit-test-item said sold out after 60,657 ms; Back on -> 1,146 ms; Hide (8 s later) -> gone from /menu after 117,461 ms. An earlier run (menu3) showed the same: /menu still served the Hidden item ('AUDIT TEST item edited ... PHP 98.50' in the HTML) for about 80 s after the save. docs/03 line 77 promises 'the menu shows a Sold Out mark within seconds'; the documented one-minute heal is for 'two saves a moment apart', which these were not. The e2e helper expectOnMenu waits up to 150 s, so the suite cannot see this.
findings.impact: STAFF-03's purpose is to stop customers ordering what ran out; for one to two minutes the item still looks available (checkout re-reads, so customers get refused late instead). A Manager who hides a wrong price or item sees it stay live and may repeat the save, which makes the race likelier.
findings.recommendation: Find the cause before tuning: log when updateTag runs versus when the 'menu' cache entry is refilled, and check whether the post-save render of /manage/menu or the item editor refills the tagged entry with pre-commit data. Cheap mitigations: shorten cacheLife for getMenu/getMenuItem to seconds for revalidate, and make the e2e check fail after about 10 s so the regression is visible.

findings.title: Two different numbers are both called 'Sales' for the same day (Orders and the Today strip vs Reports)
findings.evidence: dayOrders counts every Order not cancelled, expired or refunded (`!['cancelled','expired','refunded'].includes(o.status)`), including Placed, Accepted and Ready Pay at Pickup Orders not yet paid; salesReport counts only `status = 'picked_up'`. With my K-018 (PHP 240, Pay at Pickup, Ready) on the bar: /manage/orders showed 'Orders 12, Sales PHP 3,665' and 'Pay at Pickup still to collect PHP 240', /manage said 'Today so far 12 orders, PHP 3,665', and /manage/reports said 'Tue, Nov 10: 11, PHP 3,425'. Reports also groups by placed_at Manila day and Orders by service_day.
findings.impact: A Manager closing the day sees two Sales figures that disagree, and the larger one includes cash not yet collected, which can be mistaken for takings.
findings.recommendation: Name them differently ('Booked today' or 'Open and done' vs 'Sales, picked up') or align both on one definition from one function in the ordering module, and say on Orders that Pay at Pickup still to collect is inside the first figure.

findings.title: Busy Mode is invisible and cannot be ended outside the Bar Screen, and the Prep Time example ignores it
findings.evidence: With Busy +10 running (board: 'Busy Mode: Prep Time +10 min until 3:17 PM'; checkout: 'Ready in about 15 min ... The bar is extra busy right now'), /manage/hours had no mention of Busy (regex /busy/i false), still said 'Right now: with 4 drinks ahead, about 10 minutes.', and the /manage Today strip said 'Ordering: Taking orders'. getHoursForStaff returns prep without busyMinutes (ordering-day-db.ts:103-106) while getOrderingDay includes it; startBusyMode and endBusyMode are only reachable from bar-screen.tsx. 'Right now' is also not about now: it is a fixed 4-drink example.
findings.impact: A Manager on /manage (or on a phone, not at the bar) cannot see that times are inflated or end Busy Mode early; the Prep Time example under-states what customers are told by the Busy minutes.
findings.recommendation: Show Busy Mode (minutes and until) in the Hours page header pill and the Today strip, with Start and End controls on /manage/hours; pass busyMinutes into the example or reword it to 'Example: with 4 drinks ahead and no Busy Mode, about N minutes'.

findings.title: Blank or decimal Hours and Capacity inputs save silently: a cleared Capacity cell becomes 0 drinks, a blank map pin becomes 0,0, Prep Time is rounded
findings.evidence: `z.coerce.number()` turns '' into 0 (checked with the project's zod: blank lat -> {success:true,data:0}; capacity '' -> 0). Live: clearing Sunday 'Drinks per window' and pressing Save Capacity showed no error and capacity_rules weekday 0 became 0 (restored to 12). Prep 'Minutes per drink ahead' 1.25 saved with no message and came back as 1.3 (Decimal(4,1)); restored to 1.5. Blank Map pin latitude/longitude would save 0 (same schema; not saved live to keep cafe details intact). Special Hours accept any past date on the server (`z.iso.date`), only the date picker has min.
findings.impact: One cleared cell turns off ordering for that weekday ('No Pickup Times are left today' for every customer) with a 'Saved' message; a cleared pin moves the cafe to the Gulf of Guinea on the Visit page.
findings.recommendation: Use z.string().trim().min(1) before coercion for required numbers (or z.preprocess that maps '' to undefined), add `required` and step on the inputs, refuse more than one decimal place for Prep Time, refuse past Special Hours dates, and warn when a weekday's Capacity is 0.

findings.title: No upper bound on prices: a Base Price, Price Delta or Event price above PHP 21,474,836 crashes the editor and the typed form is lost; a typo like 1650 for 165 saves silently
findings.evidence: parsePesos accepts any safe integer, but base_cents, delta_cents and price_cents are Int (max 2,147,483,647). Live: Add a Menu Item with Base Price 99999999 -> HTTP 500, 'Something went wrong ... Something broke on our side, not yours' with React error #441, nothing saved; the same with Price Delta 99999999 on the AUDIT TEST option and Event price 99999999 on AUDIT TEST event. There is no plausibility cap, so 1650 for a PHP 165 drink saves without a warning.
findings.impact: A fat-fingered price either crashes the page and throws away every field typed, or goes live at ten times the price. Low likelihood, but it hits the core menu editor.
findings.recommendation: Cap prices in the Zod schemas (for example Base Price up to PHP 5,000, Price Delta up to PHP 500, Event price up to PHP 20,000) with a friendly message, and confirm a price change of more than 3x the old one.

findings.title: A refused cancel on /manage/orders says the Order 'can't be refunded now'
findings.evidence: cancelAction maps every failure to `done=not_allowed`, whose copy is refund copy. Live: a reason of three spaces passes the input's `required` and the server answers reason_required -> '/manage/orders?...done=not_allowed&code=K-019' showing 'K-019 can't be refunded now. It may have changed.'; cancelling K-019 again from a second tab opened before the first cancel showed the same line.
findings.impact: A Manager cancelling an Order is told about a refund that was never asked for, and is not told the real problem (no reason, or it was already cancelled).
findings.recommendation: Give cancel its own outcomes ('cancel_reason' -> 'Write a reason the Customer will see', 'cancel_not_allowed' -> 'K-019 was already cancelled or picked up'), and trim the reason before `required` (pattern=".*\S.*").

findings.title: A Barista can only mark Sold Out behind the Second Factor; the Bar Screen's 'Sold out?' link opens Annika's pending authenticator secret on the shared tablet
findings.evidence: two_factors shows annika@ with confirmed=false, created 2026-11-05 06:09: the seeded Barista has never been able to open /manage/menu. Live as Annika: /bar works; /manage and /manage/menu go to /manage/two-factor and the page title is 'Set up your authenticator' with the QR and setup key. The Bar Screen header links 'Sold out?' to /manage/menu, so on the always-signed-in tablet (ADR 0005) that link shows the Barista's pending secret to whoever is at the counter, and whoever scans it first owns her Second Factor. findings.impact: STAFF-03 (Baristas mark Sold Out) does not work in practice on the bar tablet: the Barista either enrols on a shared device or asks a Manager each time something runs out.
findings.recommendation: Offer Sold Out and Back on from the Bar Screen (a /bar Server Action limited to setMenuItemSoldOut and setOptionSoldOut, which ADR 0005 already lets the tablet do without a Second Factor), or hide the 'Sold out?' link until the Barista has enrolled on their own phone. Record the choice in a short ADR amending 0005/0014.

findings.title: Event Sign-ups are read-only for the Manager: no remove, no add for a walk-in or phone call, no 'email everyone', and unpublishing an Event tells nobody

findings.recommendation: Add Remove (with an audit row and an optional email), Add a Sign-up by hand, a 'Copy all emails' or 'Email everyone' action, and a Cancel Event action that emails confirmed Sign-ups; warn when seats go below seats taken.

findings.title: The 'Up to 50 at a time' Stars cap is only a browser attribute; a Manager can still give any amount, including to themselves

findings.impact: The UI suggests a control that does not exist; self-awarding and large awards stay possible (ID1-14).

findings.title: Reports: the 30-day view is a 30-row table with bars squeezed under the day labels, Star adjustments are netted to zero, and the 'Cancelled' and 'Refunded' links open today's Orders
findings.evidence: Last 30 days renders 30 rows newest first, 28 of them 'PHP 0' (shots/reports-30-night.png); each Bar is drawn inside the Day cell only, so its length is relative to the label column, not the row, and the trend over time has to be read bottom-up. After +51 and -51 Stars, Reports showed 'Adjusted by a Manager 0' (net), hiding 102 Stars of adjustments. The 'Cancelled' and 'Refunded' counts are over the range but link to /manage/orders, which opens today. Hero tiles use the italic display serif with tabular-nums (dataviz anti-pattern: proportional sans for hero figures). Missing for a real cafe: sales by hour (peaks for staffing and Capacity), Pay at Pickup vs online split, and a CSV export.
findings.impact: The page answers 'how much this week' but not 'when are we busy' or 'what is the trend', and the Stars panel cannot show adjustment volume, which is the number an owner would audit.
findings.recommendation: Keep the table as the table view and add one single-hue column chart oldest to newest above it (or collapse zero days); show adjustments as '+N given, -M taken'; link counts to a filtered Orders view for the range; add an hour-of-day chart and a CSV download.

findings.title: Order Codes break across lines on a landscape tablet ('K-' / '018'), and portrait tablets push Making and Ready below the fold
findings.evidence: At 1024x768 the Ready card shows the code as 'K-' on one line and '018' on the next, and 'placed 2:46 / PM' wraps (shots/bar-annika-1024x768-ready.png): the 4xl code shares a row with the right-aligned time block in a 315 px lane. At 768x1024 the lanes stack (`lg:grid-cols-3` only from 1024 px): with two New Orders the Making heading sat at y=659 and Ready at y=767 of 1024 (shots/bar-annika-768-three.png), so three or more New Orders push Ready off-screen.

findings.title: Bar cards show when an ASAP Order was placed but not when it is due, never flag late Orders, and list every default Option
findings.evidence: K-018's customer page promised 'Pickup Tue, Nov 10, 3:00 PM'; the card said 'ASAP, placed 2:46 PM' only. No card shows elapsed time or turns colour when its Pickup Window has passed. Cards print all Options, defaults included: 'Regular · Whole milk · 100% · Normal' on a plain Spanish Latte, so the one change a barista must notice is buried. Per-Order 'Running late' (8.4's dropped part) is still missing.
findings.impact: Baristas cannot see which Orders are about to miss their promised time, and deviations from the default recipe are easy to miss.

findings.title: Markdown lists and headings render unstyled in the preview and on public Event, Post and Visit pages
findings.evidence: The hint promises '- lists'. Typed '# Big heading' and '- one / - two' into the AUDIT TEST post: the preview showed plain 'Big heading' and 'one two' with no bullets (shots/post-preview.png); preview HTML has <h1> and <ul><li> but Tailwind's preflight removes list markers and heading sizes, and neither Markdown component styles them. A '#' heading also becomes a second <h1> on the public page. Raw HTML is skipped and a javascript: link becomes href="" (safe).
findings.impact: Numbered steps lose their numbers and lists look like run-on lines, so a Manager thinks the editor is broken or publishes text that reads wrong.
findings.recommendation: Style ul/ol/li/h2-h4 inside both Markdown components (one shared class), map h1 to h2, and render the preview with the same Markdown component as the public page.

findings.title: Staff page: no Second Factor status or reset, and only the 'Member' choice warns that the person is signed out
findings.evidence: Annika's enrolment has been pending since 2026-11-05 and nothing on /manage/staff shows it (rows show name, email, role). A lost phone still needs the SQL in docs/06-SETUP.md (ADR 0014 line 23). setRole ends sessions whenever the rank drops (`RANK[role] < RANK[person.role]`), so Manager -> Barista signs the person out, but the warning 'They lose staff access and are signed out now.' appears only for Member; the Add Staff form gives no hint when the email already belongs to a Manager, so 'Give role' with the default Barista demotes and signs them out. Read from code; the role change itself was not exercised (blocked).
findings.impact: Managers cannot see who still has to enrol or help someone who lost a phone, and can demote a colleague by accident.
findings.recommendation: Show 'Authenticator: set up / waiting' per person and a Manager-only 'Reset authenticator' (deletes the two_factors row and ends sessions, audited), as ADR 0014 could be amended to allow. Warn on any change that lowers a role, and in Add Staff say 'already a Manager' before saving.

findings.title: 'Sign out everywhere' copy promises 'at once', but the Bar Screen keeps working for up to 5 minutes
findings.evidence: auth.ts:19 `cookieCache: { enabled: true, maxAge: 5 * 60 }` with the comment 'a sign-out elsewhere takes effect within 5 minutes'. endSessions deletes session rows, but /bar and /api/bar call getSession, which trusts the signed cookie until it expires, and the Bar Screen needs no Second Factor row lookup; /manage pages do re-read the session row (secondFactorPassed) so they react at once. Role removal is immediate because the role is re-read from the database. Copy: 'Taking a role away signs them out at once' and 'They are signed out on every phone and computer'. Not run live: the AUDIT TEST Barista could not be created.
findings.impact: After a Manager signs out a lost or stolen tablet, it can keep moving Orders for up to five minutes.
findings.recommendation: Say 'within 5 minutes' in the copy, or make /api/bar and requireStaff on /bar look the session row up (the cost is one indexed read per 3 s poll), or disable the cookie cache for Staff.

findings.title: A Pay at Pickup refund records no Refund row and never tells the Manager to hand the cash back
findings.evidence: Refunded my picked-up Pay at Pickup K-018: the confirm said 'Refund PHP 240 in full?' and the result 'Refunded K-018. The Customer sees it on their Order page.'; refundPayment returns 'no_online_payment' with no Payment, so the refunds table has 0 rows for K-018 (who refunded is only in order_events).
findings.impact: Nothing prompts the cash hand-back, and cash refunds are missing from any refund list or reconciliation.
findings.recommendation: For Pay at Pickup say 'Give PHP 240 back in cash, then confirm', and record a cash Refund row (provider 'cash') so refunds are in one place.

findings.title: Closing a day on Opening Hours still demands its opening, last-order and closing times
findings.evidence: WeeklyRow requires all three times even when isClosed is true. Ticking 'Sunday closed' with its Opens field cleared gave 'Sunday: Enter opening, last order and closing.' and 'Some fields need a fix.'; nothing saved. The CSS greys the times out when Closed is ticked, which suggests they are not needed.
findings.impact: Small friction and a confusing message when closing a weekday.
findings.recommendation: Make the times optional when isClosed (keep the old values), as Special Hours already does.

findings.title: The Barista Pick limit counts Hidden and seasonal-ended items and does not say which three hold the slots
findings.evidence: The count is `db.menuItem.count({ where: { badges: { has: pick } ... } })` with no isHidden or availableUntil filter, while Home shows picks from getMenu (visible items only). Live: ticking Day Barista Pick on a new Hidden item gave 'Three Day Barista Picks already. Untick one of them first.' without naming Ube Pandesal, Hoshi Latte and Tablea Tsokolate.
findings.impact: A hidden or ended item can silently hold a pick, so Home shows two picks and the Manager is told the slots are full.
findings.recommendation: Count only visible, in-season items and list the current picks with links in the error.

findings.title: Submitting the sign-in form quickly after the page loads drops ?next=, so Staff land on /account instead of /bar or /manage
findings.evidence: Two scripted sign-ins that typed and submitted right after load (networkidle) posted next=/account and the emailed links carried callbackURL=%2Faccount (Christian with ?next=%2Fmanage, the AUDIT account with ?next=%2Fbar); two that waited 3 s more posted /bar and landed on /bar. Sampling the hidden field every 50 ms never showed /account, so the cause is unclear (possibly a submit before the streamed form is hydrated). The Bar Screen's 'Sign in again' link and every requireStaff redirect rely on next.
findings.impact: Staff returning to the tablet land on their account page and must find the Bar Screen again; minor.
findings.recommendation: Reproduce with a slowed network; if confirmed, keep next in the URL the action reads (headers referer) or render the hidden field server-side outside the streamed boundary.

refs: findings-2026-11-10 motion: The Bar Screen makes a new AudioContext for every chime and never closes it
findings.title: The new-Order chime may stay silent after the tablet reloads until someone taps the screen
findings.evidence: chime() creates a new AudioContext on each new Order and never calls resume(). Browser autoplay policy creates an AudioContext in the 'suspended' state when the page has had no user activation, and the try/catch hides it. In headless Chromium (even with --autoplay-policy=document-user-activation-required) the context reported 'running', so this was not reproduced.
findings.impact: After a morning reload or a crash, the first Orders arrive without sound until a barista touches the board.
findings.recommendation: Create one AudioContext on the first tap of 'Sound for new orders' (or any tap), resume() it before playing, and show 'Tap to turn on sound' while its state is suspended.
